# Testing Best Practices

> Proven patterns for test configuration, coverage, and test architecture across frameworks.

## Entries

- [Vitest Configuration for Monorepos](vitest-monorepo-config.md): Per-package Vitest configs with Turborepo orchestration. RECOMMENDED.
- [Playwright E2E Testing](playwright-e2e.md): Cross-browser E2E testing with auto-start dev server. OPTIONAL.
- [Split side-effect-free data out of a module that mutates the DOM at import time](browser-side-effect-free-data-extraction.md): extract a pure data constant into its own module when its current home also runs document/window-touching bootstrap code at import time, so a Node/vitest test can import the data without crashing on a missing DOM. RECOMMENDED.
- [Use a dynamic await import() inside beforeAll, not a static import, when a test sets an env var to override a module's load-time config](dynamic-import-for-env-override-hermetic-tests.md): static imports are hoisted above a test file's own process.env assignment, so the module-under-test silently captures the wrong config; loading it dynamically inside beforeAll fixes it. RECOMMENDED.
- [Verify prod-only static UI pre-deploy with a scratchpad harness server + DevTools emulation](static-harness-server-for-prod-only-ui.md): a throwaway no-dep static server rooted at the app's public dir plus a scratchpad harness page mounting the real modules with worst-case fake state, measured numerically under true device emulation. RECOMMENDED.
- [Alias absolute browser-style imports in vitest.config.ts, don't rewrite them to relative](vitest-alias-unbundled-browser-imports.md): unbundled frontends use absolute imports like "/shared/util.js" that Node/vitest cannot resolve; map those prefixes to filesystem paths via resolve.alias instead of rewriting source imports to relative. RECOMMENDED.
- [Reproduce load-dependent test flakes under forced CPU contention, and measure before/after at the same load](stress-harness-for-load-dependent-flakes.md): a flake that only fails in a full suite may never reproduce on an idle machine (green 6/6 before the fix, but failing 1 of 2 under 64 spinners), so saturate the CPU deliberately, baseline BEFORE changing anything, and verify at the same hog count -- a green run at normal load was the starting condition and proves nothing. RECOMMENDED.
- [Test SELECT-only SQL read-only against a real database by shadowing tables with CTEs](cte-shadow-read-only-sql-tests.md): prefix fixture CTEs named after the real tables to every statement, run inside BEGIN READ ONLY, and refuse unshadowed tables, so production SQL is exercised with no DDL or writes and can be verified against any database, even prod. RECOMMENDED.
- [When you cannot attach the vendor's extension, re-implement it and test parity against the real one](parity-test-against-the-vendor-sdk-when-you-cannot-use-it.md): When a vendor extension cannot be attached and you re-implement it, run the vendor's version on the same input in a test and assert equal answers. RECOMMENDED.
- [Prove an access-preserving refactor by dumping the full viewer matrix before and after and diffing it](access-matrix-diff-for-permission-refactors.md): enumerate every role and level combination, dump what each viewer gets on the commit before and after, require byte-identical output, then keep exact-set and full-walk assertions in the suite. RECOMMENDED.
- [Test database code through two pools: a privileged one to set up, the restricted runtime role to assert](test-database-code-through-two-pools-privileged-setup-restricted-runtime-role.md): run the migrator as the schema-owner role and assert only through a second pool as the NOBYPASSRLS runtime role, so row-level security, grants and function ownership are actually exercised. RECOMMENDED.
- [Confirm every new test fails without its fix](confirm-every-new-test-fails-without-its-fix.md): revert the fix, run only that test, require the intended failure, restore; and mutation-test SQL policy checks with a small script of deliberate schema defects. A test that has only ever passed has proved nothing. RECOMMENDED.
- [Review each layer with an independent security pass before building the next layer on it](independent-security-review-per-layer.md): a reviewer who did not write the layer and is not given the authors' conclusions looks for blockers and reads the tests as claims; in the source build every pass found a blocker that the authors' own tests had codified as intended behaviour. RECOMMENDED.
